spots.name: Maiden Tower
spots.summary: The Maiden Tower is a 12th-century monument in the Old City, Baku, Azerbaijan. Along with the Shirvanshahs' Palace, dated to the 15th century, it forms a group of historic monuments listed in 2001 under the UNESCO World Heritage List of Historical Monuments as cultural property, Category III.

spots.name: Old City
spots.summary: Old City or Inner City is the historical core of Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan. The Old City is the most ancient part of Baku, which is surrounded by walls. In 2007, the Old City had a population of about 3,000 people.

spots.name: Palace of the Shirvanshahs
spots.summary: The Palace of the Shirvanshahs is a 15th-century palace built by the Shirvanshahs and described by UNESCO as "one of the pearls of Azerbaijan's architecture".

spots.name: State Flag Square
spots.summary: State Flag Square is a public square situated along Neftchiler Avenue in Bayil, Baku, Azerbaijan. Spanning 60 hectares, with its upper section covering 3 hectares, the square prominently displays national symbols of Azerbaijan, including the state coat of arms, anthem, and a bronze map of the country.

spots.name: Baku Fortress Wall
spots.summary: Baku Fortress is a medieval building in Baku, Azerbaijan, the largest of Absheron fortresses. The fortress consists of the Icheri Sheher and the walls and towers surrounding it, and it was included by UNESCO into the World Cultural Heritage List in 2000.

spots.name: Bibi-Heybat Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Bibi-Heybat Mosque is located in the village of Bibiheybət, near Baku, Azerbaijan. The current structure, completed in the 1990s, replicates the original 13th-century mosque built at the behest of Iranian Shirvanshah Farrukhzad II Ibn Ahsitan II.

spots.name: Azerbaijan Carpet Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Azerbaijan National Carpet Museum is a museum located in Baku that displays Azerbaijani carpets and rugs with historical and modern weaving techniques and materials. It has the largest collection of Azerbaijani carpets in the world.

spots.name: Baku Boulevard
spots.summary: Baku Boulevard is a promenade established in 1909 which runs parallel to Baku's seafront. Its history goes back more than 100 years, to a time when Baku oil barons built their mansions along the Caspian shore and when the seafront was artificially built up inch by inch.

spots.name: National Art Museum of Azerbaijan

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Azerbaijan National Museum of Art is the biggest art museum of Azerbaijan. It was founded in 1936 in Baku and in 1943 was named after Rustam Mustafayev, a prominent Azerbaijani scenic designer and theater artist. The museum consists of two 19th-century buildings standing next to each other.

spots.name: National Museum of History of Azerbaijan

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The National Museum of History of Azerbaijan is the largest museum in Azerbaijan. It is located in Baku, in the former residential house of Azerbaijani oil magnate and philanthropist Haji Zeynalabdin Taghiyev. The museum was founded in 1920, following the Russian takeover of Baku, and opened to visitors in 1921.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of History of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Juma Mosque, Baku

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Juma Mosque, also known as the Friday Mosque, is a Shia Islam mosque, located in Baku, Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Baku railway station
spots.summary: Baku railway station is the central station of Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan. It is located in the Nesimi district in central Baku, approximately 3 km northeast from the historical core of Baku, İçərişəhər. This station is located in the city Transport HUB.

photo.author: Press Service of the President of the Republic of Azerbaijan

spots.name: Church of the Holy Virgin

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of the Holy Virgin or Holy Mother of God Church was an Armenian Apostolic church in the Old City (İçərişəhər) of Baku, Azerbaijan, built in the 18th century and demolished in 1992.

spots.name: Muhammad Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Muhammad Mosque or Siniggala Mosque is a former mosque, located in the Old City of Baku, Azerbaijan. The mosque was built in the 11th century.

spots.name: Martyrs' Lane
spots.summary: Martyrs' Lane or Alley of Martyrs, formerly known as the Kirov Park, is a cemetery and memorial in Baku, Azerbaijan dedicated to those killed by the Soviet Army during Black January 1990 and in the First Nagorno-Karabakh War of 1988–1994.

spots.name: Nizami Museum of Azerbaijani Literature

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National museum of Azerbaijan literature, named after Nizami Ganjavi is a museum in Baku, established in 1939. It is located near the entrance of Icheri Sheher, not far from the Fountains Square. The museum is considered one of the greatest and richest treasuries of Azerbaijani culture.

spots.name: Fountains Square, Baku
spots.summary: Fountains Square is a public square in downtown Baku, capital of Azerbaijan. The square was previously called Parapet and is often referenced as the same name now. The name of the fountains square derives from the presence of dozens of fountains throughout the square first constructed during Soviet rule of Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Multani Caravanserai
spots.summary: The Multani Caravanserai is a caravanserai located in Baku, Azerbaijan. It was established in the 14th century and is located in the Icherisheher old town, opposite the Bukhara Caravanserai.

spots.name: Nizami Street
spots.summary: Nizami Street, commonly known as Tarqovu or Tarqovi, is a large pedestrian and shopping street in downtown Baku, Azerbaijan, named after the classical Azerbaijani poet Nizami Ganjavi.

spots.name: Ismailiyya Palace
spots.summary: The Ismailiyya Palace is a historical building that currently serves as the Presidium of the Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan. It is on Istiglaliyyat Street in Baku.

spots.name: Church of the Saviour

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Saviour is a Lutheran church located at 28 May Street in Baku, Azerbaijan. Built between 1896 and 1899, it was designed in the Gothic Revival style by architect Adolf Eichler.

spots.name: Baku Museum of Miniature Books

hours.note: Closed Mon, Thu

spots.summary: The Baku Museum of Miniature Books is the only museum of miniature books in the world, settled in the old part of Baku, called Inner City. The museum opened on 2 April 2002.

spots.name: Palatial mosque in Baku

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palatial mosque in Baku, also known as the Palace Mosque, and Shirvanshahs Palace Mosque, is a mosque, located inside the Palace of the Shirvanshahs complex, in the Old City of Baku, Azerbaijan. The mosque was built in 845 AH (1441/1442 CE) by the Iranian Shirvanshahs.

spots.name: Armenian Church, Baku

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Gregory the Illuminator Church, commonly referred to as the Armenian Church of Baku, is a former Armenian Apostolic church near Fountains Square in central Baku, Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Taza Pir Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Taza Pir Mosque is a Shia Islam mosque, located in Baku, Azerbaijan. Its construction began in 1905 and was finished by 1914. The concept for the mosque as well as its financing was provided by an Azeri female philanthropist, Nabat Khanum Ashurbeyova (Ashurbeyli).

spots.name: Bukhara Caravanserai
spots.summary: Bukhara Caravanserai is a caravanserai located in Baku, Azerbaijan. It was erected in the late 15th century over a trade route passing through the Shamakhi Gates of the fortress. It is located in the Icherisheher old town, opposite the Multani Caravanserai, and close to the Maiden Tower.

spots.name: Ashur Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ashur Mosque, also known as the Lezgi Mosque, is a Sunni Islam mosque in the Old City of Baku, Azerbaijan. It was founded in 1169 by the master Najaf Ashur son of Ibrahim. It is located in Asaf Zeynalli Street. The mosque was closed for repairs in 2016 and as of December 2024, the mosque remains closed.

spots.name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Alexander Nevsky Cathedral was the main Russian Orthodox cathedral in Baku, Azerbaijan from its completion in 1898 until its destruction in 1937 during the Soviet era under Joseph Stalin. The cathedral was the biggest Russian Orthodox structure ever built in the South Caucasus.

spots.name: Azerbaijan State Academic Opera and Ballet Theater
spots.summary: The Azerbaijan State Academic Opera and Ballet Theater is an opera house in Baku, Azerbaijan. Formerly known as the Mailov Theatre, was designed in 1911 by Armenian architect Nikolai Bayev at the request of the Armenian magnate Daniel Mailov, one of the Mailov brothers.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Azerbaijan State Academic Opera and Ballet Theater

spots.name: Jinn Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Jinn Mosque is a former mosque, located on Gala turn, in the Palace of the Shirvanshahs in the Old City of Baku, in Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Bazar Square
spots.summary: Bazar square or Khanagah complex is a historic religious-architectural complex with arcade of the 12-13th centuries. It is a part of Old City and located on Kichik Gala street, in the city of Baku, in Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Shirvanshahs' Palace Mausoleum
spots.summary: Shirvanshahs' Palace Mausoleum or Tomb of the Shirvanshahs' family is a historical monument of the 15th century. Located in Old City, it is a part of the Palace of the Shirvanshahs complex.

spots.name: Palace of Happiness
spots.summary: The Palace of Happiness, currently also called Palace of Marriage Registrations and previously called Mukhtarov Palace, is a historic building in the center of Baku, Azerbaijan, built in Neo-Gothic style in the early 20th century by Polish architect Józef Płoszko.

spots.name: Azerbaijan State Philharmonic Hall
spots.summary: The Muslim Magomayev Azerbaijan State Academic Philharmonic Hall, located in Baku, is a concert hall in Azerbaijan. Since 2006 Murad Adigozalzade is the director of the Azerbaijan State Academic Philharmonic Hall.

spots.name: Baku Funicular
spots.summary: Baku Funicular is a funicular system in Baku, Azerbaijan. It connects a square on Neftchilar Avenue and Martyrs' Lane. It is the first and remains the only funicular system in the country.

spots.name: Statue of a Liberated Woman
spots.summary: Statue of a Liberated Woman is a statue by Fuad Abdurahmanov in Baku, Azerbaijan. It was built in 1960 at the Public Square at the intersection of Gurbanov and Jafar Jabbarly streets in Yasamal raion, and was inspired by the character of Sevil from Jafar Jabbarly's play Sevil.

spots.name: Chin Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chin Mosque, also known as the Gazi Fezlullah bin Osman Mosque, is a historical former mosque, located on Kichik Gala street, near the Palace of the Shirvanshahs, in the Old City of Baku, in Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Beyler Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Beyler Mosque is a former Shia Islam mosque and historic architectural monument which is located in the Old City of Baku, opposite the “Murad” Gate of the Shirvanshah Palace Complex, in Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Azadliq Square
spots.summary: Azadliq Square, in Baku is the biggest city-center square in Azerbaijan. It lies next to Baku Boulevard.

spots.name: Church of Michael the Archangel, Baku

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of Michael the Archangel or Flotskaya is a Russian Orthodox church located at the intersection of Vidadi and Zargarpalan streets in the Yasamal district, central Baku, Azerbaijan. It is under the jurisdiction of the Baku Eparchy and dedicated to Archangel Michael.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Church of Michael the Archangel, Baku

spots.name: Divankhana
spots.summary: The Divankhana is a rotunda pavilion built on a tall stylobate in the north-west of the Shirvanshahs Palace, located in the historic Old City of Baku, in Azerbaijan. In the fifteenth century, Shirvanshah was built by order of Farrukh Yasar. Several stories describe the Divan's operation.

spots.name: Philharmonic Garden
spots.summary: Filarmoniya Bağı, sometimes called Gubernator's or Governor's Park, is a park in Baku, Azerbaijan, next to Baku fortress.

photo.author: Photo by MrArifnajafov (Photography from the original).

spots.name: Istiglaliyyat Street
spots.summary: Istiglaliyyat Street is an arterial road in the central uptown part of Baku, Azerbaijan. It begins at Gulustan Palace, located on the southern hillside part of Baku, and continues north, then northeast, terminating at the intersection of Aziz Aliyev and Mammad Amin Rasulzade Streets at the edge of Fountains Square.

spots.name: Government House
spots.summary: The Government House of Baku, also known as the House of Government, is a government building housing various state ministries of Azerbaijan. It is located on Neftchiler Avenue and faces the Baku Boulevard, while the rear of the building faces the busy Uzeyir Hajibeyov Street in central Baku.

spots.name: Keygubad Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Keygubad Mosque is a historical former mosque, now in partial ruins, located on Gala turn in the Old City of Baku in Azerbaijan. The 14th century former mosque is on the south side of the mausoleum of Seyid Yahya Bakuvi.

spots.name: Building of the Baku City Executive Power

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Building of Baku City Executive Power is an administrative building in Azerbaijan's capital Baku, at Istiglaliyyat Street, 4. The building was built in Baroque style in 1900–1904 on the basis of Polish architect Józef Gosławski's project. The building is the last work of Gosławski.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Building of the Baku City Executive Power

spots.name: Mausoleum of Seyid Yahya Bakuvi
spots.summary: The Mausoleum of Seyid Yahya Bakuvi was built in approximately 1457–1458, in the Old City of Baku, Azerbaijan. The mausoleum is located in the centre of the middle yard of the Palace of the Shirvanshahs.

spots.name: Two-Storeyed Caravanserai
spots.summary: Two-storeyed caravanserai or Gasim bey caravanserai is a historic monument of the XV century. It is a part of Old City and located on Hagigat Rzayeva street, in the city of Baku, in Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Baku Khans' Palace
spots.summary: Baku Khans' Palace is a complex of several houses that belonged to the members of the ruling family of the Baku Khanate.

spots.name: Saint Bartholomew Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Bartholomew Church was a church that existed in the Old City of Baku, Azerbaijan.

spots.name: National Library of Azerbaijan

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Library of Azerbaijan, officially named the Mirza Fatali Akhundov National Library of Azerbaijan after Mirza Fatali Akhundov, is the national library of the Republic of Azerbaijan, located in Baku and founded in 1923. It is named after Mirza Fatali Akhundov, an Azerbaijani dramatist and philosopher.

spots.name: Holy Myrrhbearers Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Holy Myrrhbearers Cathedral is a local historical monument and church, built in 1909 in Baku, Azerbaijan. It serves as the center of the Baku diocese.

spots.name: Aliagha Vahid Monument
spots.summary: Aliagha Vahid Monument is a monument in Baku, capital of Azerbaijan, in honor of the Azerbaijani poet and ghazal singer Aliagha Vahid (1895–1965). It was built in 1990.

spots.name: Molla Ahmad Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Molla Ahmad Mosque, also known as the Nasir ad-Din Gashtasib Mosque, is a former mosque, located on Sabir street, in the Icherisheher of Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Mosque of the Martyrs

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Mosque of the Martyrs or Martyrs' Mosque, officially the Alley of Martyrs' Mosque, also known as the Turkish Mosque and Shahid's Mosque, is a Sunni Islam mosque, located near the Martyrs' Lane, in the Upland Park district of Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Museum of Archaeology and Ethnography

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology, located in Baku, Azerbaijan. Exhibition Hall of the Institute of Archaeology and Anthropology, Azerbaijan National Academy of Sciences.

spots.name: Neftchiler Avenue
spots.summary: Neftchiler Avenue is an arterial road in Baku, Azerbaijan. It begins at the west end of the Bayil district of Baku and continues east until terminating at Javanshir Bridge, intersecting Uzeyir Hajibeyov Street.

spots.name: Monument to Muslim Magomayev
spots.summary: The Monument to Muslim Magomayev is a sculptural work of the Azerbaijani sculptor and artist Omar Eldarov, dedicated to the Azerbaijani and Soviet opera, pop singer, People's Artist of the USSR Muslim Magomayev.

spots.name: Khidir Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Khidir Mosque is a former mosque, located on Muslim Magomayev street, in the Old City of Baku, in Azerbaijan.

spots.name: Palace of Zeynalabdin Taghiyev
spots.summary: Palace of Zeynalabdin Taghiyev – Baku, H.Z. Taghiyev Street 4, previously owned by Baku millionaire Zeynalabdin Taghiyev, and now the palace building houses the National Museum of History of Azerbaijan. The building was constructed in 1893–1902 by Polish civil engineer Józef Gosławski.

spots.name: International Mugham Center of Azerbaijan
spots.summary: This is the center of Azerbaijani arts and music dedicated to promote, preserve and popularize the Azerbaijani music genre Mugam. The center covers 7,500 m² and has 3 stories. The design of the building was based on elements and shapes of Tar, an Azerbaijani musical instrument used in performing Mugham. The concert hall has a capacity of 350 people.
